narrative.title: Quarantining Corrupted Rows in a Grid Telemetry Board
narrative.scenario: A monitoring board stores sensor readings on a rectangular grid. A node reading exactly zero means the bus is faulty, and any row or column containing such a reading must be wiped to zeros to avoid propagating bad data. Perform the wipe in place with constant extra space, without cascading wipes caused by your own edits.
narrative.inputFormat: An m x n matrix of integers.
narrative.outputFormat: The same matrix with every element of any row or column that originally contained a zero set to 0.
constraints: The wipe must happen in place with constant extra space

testCases.explanation: The faulty node lies in the middle, so its entire row and column become zeros.
Two faulty readings wipe rows 0 and the first and last columns, leaving only the interior cells intact.

hintLevels: Level 1: You need to remember which rows and columns are doomed before changing anything, but a full boolean array per axis uses extra space.
Level 2: The first row and first column can serve as the marker storage: record a zero hit in the row's leading cell and the column's top cell.

Level 3: Because the first row and column double as storage, their own original zero status must be captured up front and applied last, and the marking pass must skip row 0 and column 0 to avoid self-triggering.
